props.title: *batteries not included
props.initialSlug: Tiny alien robots help save a NYC apartment building

sections.content: batteries not included (1987) stands as a charming blend of urban drama and sci-fi whimsy, emerging during a fertile period of Spielberg-produced family films. Like Short Circuit (1986) and E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), it centers on the relationship between humans and mechanical beings, but uniquely focuses on elderly protagonists fighting gentrification. The tiny flying UFOs that assist the residents of a condemned apartment building represent both technological wonder and a metaphor for community resilience, themes that would later influence films like WALL-E (2008) and Hugo (2011).

sections.content: Director Matthew Robbins, working from a story co-written by Brad Bird (later of The Iron Giant (1999) fame), crafts a distinctly urban fairy tale. The film's practical effects hold up remarkably well, with the "fix-it" flying saucers created by Industrial Light & Magic bringing personality and charm to what could have been cold mechanical creatures. Jessica Tandy and Hume Cronyn's performances as the elderly couple at the heart of the story ground the fantastic elements in genuine human emotion.

The film's setting in a decaying East Village neighborhood provides commentary on 1980s urban renewal and displacement that remains relevant today. Like Batteries Not Included (1987), later films such as District 9 (2009) and Attack the Block (2011) would use science fiction elements to explore urban social issues, though with decidedly darker tones. sections.content: The film's masterful combination of practical effects and puppetry represents a high point in pre-CGI filmmaking. The miniature flying saucers were achieved through a combination of rod puppetry, stop motion, and radio-controlled models - techniques that would influence films like Gremlins (1984) and Howard the Duck (1986). This tangible approach to effects work creates a tactile quality that many modern viewers find more engaging than pure CGI.
